agent_notes: The last clause (yafiach lo) is the hardest crux of the psalm. KJV 'from him that puffeth at him', ASV 'the safety he panteth for', YLT 'him who doth breathe for it'. I read 'I will set [him] in the safety [for which] he pants'; this follows the ASV and the Hebrew's 'for it' (lo). Rashi in the packet reads yafiach as 'speaks', Radak as 'snare' (from Prov 29:8), and Meiri's own view is 'fights'. The literal layer keeps the ambiguity in brackets.

agent_notes: Reviewer request applied: the commentary no longer says the KJV softens 'this generation'. It says KJV and ASV level singular 'him' (titzerenu) into 'them', and that YLT reads 'us'. Whom the singular points to is read from Radak ('each and every poor person'); the 'them' is the poor of v.6, as Rashi, Radak, Meiri and Metzudat David have it. Ibn Ezra and Malbim see the words of v.7 as the antecedent of the first verb; I mention that only briefly.
'zu' for the near demonstrative before the noun is a poetic form of zeh/zo; the 'this generation' is read as the speaker's own age, per Radak and Metzudat David.
